requirements.requirement: One spike in the same cell
requirements.evidence: spike:0#-1,0|-1,1|0,0 stands at one corner of cell (-1,1), where it meets cells (-1,0) and (0,0).

requirements.requirement: Drawer and spike at the very same corner, touching
requirements.evidence: The spike was refused at the drawer's corner (junction -1,1 | 0,0 | 0,1) with SPIKE_CLASH: the drawer fills that corner. The spike is at a different corner of the same cell, so the two don't touch.

finish.summary: The configurator won't put a drawer and a spike at the same corner of one cell. I built a drawer on half base (-1,1) and a spike at that cell's nearest corner it allows (the other end of the side the drawer cell shares with base 0,0), not the drawer's corner, so the two don't touch. I put a third base at (0,1) to make the drawer's corner a meeting point of three cells, then tried the spike there. It was refused with SPIKE_CLASH: the drawer fills the south half of the cell, which is where the spike would stand. I then took that base off and placed the spike at the allowed corner. Open faces are capped and the joints are bolted. check_build found no problems and no part collisions. The build has 17 parts.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
